# Setup guide: which way suits you?

<!-- Generated by tools/build-setup-guide.mjs from public/js/lib/setup-scenes.js and the catalogs. Do not edit by hand. -->

[Deutsch](../../einstieg/wegweiser.md) · **English**

[← Compendium index](../README.md)

This shows how the parts fit together. **The ways are building blocks, not levels:** take one, combine several or stay with the one that is enough for you. Home Assistant and AI are options, not requirements.

The app has the same guide under **Help → Setup guide**, with the quick choice to tap. The setup assistant asks the same three questions. The steps are in the linked guides; this page only shows the way.

## Quick choice

| Question | Answer | Way |
|---|---|---|
| Do you have smart meters or Home Assistant? | Yes | [With Home Assistant](#weg-home-assistant) |
| Do you want supplier mail read for you? | Yes | [With supplier mail](#weg-inbox) |
| Do you want to ask an AI, and may anything leave your home? | Yes, only at home | [With local AI](#weg-local-ai) |
| Do you want to ask an AI, and may anything leave your home? | Yes, it may leave | [With cloud AI (experimental)](#weg-cloud-ai) |
| Two or more of these | | [All together](#weg-together) |
| None of these | | [By hand](#weg-by-hand) |

Saying no to all of these is a good answer. “By hand” is a complete way of working.

<a id="weg-by-hand"></a>

## By hand

You read your meters and enter the readings, in a browser or on your phone.

<picture><source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="../../ui/wegweiser/by-hand.en.narrow.svg"><img src="../../ui/wegweiser/by-hand.en.svg" alt="Diagram: By hand" width="760"></picture>

**Inside your home**

- Your meters → You: you read them
- You → Energietracker: enter the reading
- Energietracker → You: consumption, costs, deadlines

**Across the boundary of your home**

- Energietracker → Weather service: rounded location, can be switched off

**Who it is for:** For anyone who reads their own meters and needs no further technology at home.

**What you get**

- Consumption and costs per utility, compared with the previous year.
- **The balance:** will you pay more, or get something back?
- Forecast, deadlines and notes on your contracts.
- Bill checks and the annual report.

**What you need**

- Software: The Energietracker, most easily as a Docker container, otherwise on a NAS or web server with PHP 8.2 or later. Plus an up-to-date browser.
- Hardware: **A computer or NAS on your home network.** A phone is enough for entering readings.

**Effort:** **Set it up once:** the “First steps” guide allows about 15 minutes. After that you only enter readings, as often as you like. Two readings give the first consumption figure.

**Steps**

1. Start the Energietracker. [Docker](../betrieb/docker.md) · [Web server and PHP](../betrieb/installation.md)
2. **Go through the setup:** language and country, who you are, which energy sources you use. [Setup, example households and levels](einrichtung.md)
3. Enter the first reading. (in the app: **Meter readings**)
4. Add your contract so that costs and balance are right. (in the app: **Contracts & payments**)
5. **Set your location:** the app needs the weather for heating degree days and the forecast. (in the app: **Weather data**)
6. Add your phone if you want to enter readings at the meter. [Using it on your phone](handy.md)

**Where your data stays:** **Everything is stored as files on your server, with no account and no telemetry.** Only the weather sync goes out: your location, rounded to about 1 km, to Open-Meteo. You can switch it off under Connections → Weather data. The place search only asks there when you use it.

**What it cannot do**

- **Between two readings the app spreads consumption evenly over the days.** It does not measure, and it says which figure is spread.
- **No quarter-hours:** assessing flexibility and storage takes values per quarter-hour.
- **Nothing arrives by itself:** without a new entry the figures stay as they were.

**In detail:** **Docker packs the Energietracker with everything it needs into a container.** Your data stays outside it, in the folder you mount.

**Addresses and ports**

- Docker: `http://energietracker.local:8080`. Port 8080 on the computer leads to port 80 in the container.
- Apache, nginx, Synology Web Station: `http://energietracker.local/energietracker/`. **Under the folder where you put the app.** Apache uses the included `.htaccess`.

**Starting with Docker**

```text
docker run -d --name energietracker \
  --restart unless-stopped -p 8080:80 \
  -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  ghcr.io/bingerminger/energietracker:3
```

**Good to know**

- **Everything is in `/data` in the container, here in the `data` folder next to the command.** You can also back up in the app: Settings → Data and backup.
- The image is available for amd64 and arm64, so also for computers with an ARM processor.
- **Without sign-in, anyone who can reach the address can read and change everything.** Switch sign-in on under Settings → Access and security.
- **Opening it as an app on the home screen and without a network takes HTTPS.** In a browser on your home network it works without.

**Common errors**

- Port 8080 is in use: Choose another port on the computer, such as `-p 9000:80`.
- Data gone after `docker rm`: **No folder was mounted.** Always start with `-v`, using a folder or a named volume.
- Docker Desktop: error `mounts denied`: **The folder is not shared.** Share it under `Settings → Resources → File sharing` or use `-v energietracker-data:/data`.
- Image without root: `/api/health` answers `503`: The data folder does not belong to the container’s UID: `sudo chown -R 10001:0 ./data` or a named volume.

[Docker](../betrieb/docker.md) · [Web server and PHP](../betrieb/installation.md) · [Troubleshooting](../betrieb/fehlersuche.md)

<a id="weg-inbox"></a>

## With supplier mail

PDF into the inbox. You check what was read and take it over.

<picture><source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="../../ui/wegweiser/inbox.en.narrow.svg"><img src="../../ui/wegweiser/inbox.en.svg" alt="Diagram: With supplier mail" width="760"></picture>

**Inside your home**

- Supplier mail → Energietracker: drop the PDF
- Energietracker → AI at home: text of the document
- AI at home → Energietracker: proposal with its source passage
- You → Energietracker: you check and take it over

**Across the boundary of your home**

- Energietracker → Cloud service: only the document, after your consent
- Energietracker → Weather service: rounded location, can be switched off

**Who it is for:** For anyone who has bills and contract letters as PDFs and does not want to type them in. Works without AI too: the inbox is then the place to file your mail.

**What you get**

- Contracts, bills, meters and readings from the document, every field with its literal source passage and page.
- **One sentence for each document:** what the letter means for you and what to do now.
- A file on every contract and meter with all its documents.
- On a price change, a note on your rights.

**What you need**

- Software: **The Energietracker is enough for filing.** To read documents, your own service on your home network (Ollama or OpenAI-compatible such as LM Studio) or a cloud service (experimental).
- Hardware: **For local reading, a computer on which a language model runs smoothly.** Filing works from any device.

**Effort:** **Filing works right away.** To read documents you install a service, load a model and enter the address, or choose a provider and key in the cloud. You check every document yourself, and locally it takes a while; the guide says how long.

**Steps**

1. Put the first PDF into the inbox. (in the app: **Inbox**)
2. **If it should be read:** set up local or cloud under Connections → Reading mail and photos. (in the app: **Reading mail and photos**) · [Setting up reading](../anleitungen/posteingang.md#setting-up-reading)
3. Check the proposal next to the document and take it over. [Preview and taking over](../anleitungen/posteingang.md#preview-and-taking-over)
4. Bring in mail in other ways too, if you like. [Other ways in](../anleitungen/posteingang.md#other-ways-into-the-inbox)

**Where your data stays:** **The PDF stays on your server and travels with every backup.** Locally, only the text goes to your service on your home network. In the cloud, every document you send for reading goes to the chosen service, including name, address and numbers; the app asks first and sends nothing without your consent. No other data of your household leaves. The weather sync is the same for every way.

**What it cannot do**

- **The inbox does not read photos and scans without a text layer.** You enter those by hand.
- PDF only, up to 10 MB per file.
- **Without a service set up, nothing reads along.** You then file, assign and enter by hand.
- **The AI only proposes.** What you confirm is taken over.

**In detail:** **The browser reads the PDF’s text layer and sends it to your server.** The server sends it, without the pages of terms and conditions, to your service. Its address must be on your own network; the app checks this on every call.

**Addresses and ports**

- Local with Ollama: `http://mein-rechner.local:11434`. From inside a container, Ollama must listen on the network: `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`.
- Local, OpenAI-compatible (such as LM Studio): `http://mein-rechner.local:1234/v1`. The address goes up to and including `/v1`.
- Filing a PDF from outside the app: `http://energietracker.local:8080/api/inbox?name=rechnung.pdf`. With a key; shortcuts and email via Home Assistant use the same entrance.

**Filing with curl**

```text
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer etk_…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" \
  --data-binary @rechnung.pdf \
  "http://energietracker.local:8080/api/inbox?name=rechnung.pdf"
```

**Good to know**

- The watched folder is called `posteingang/` and lives in the data directory.
- **Only people who manage the installation may set up reading.** The card has its own save button.
- **All cloud routes are experimental:** they have not yet been tested with real feedback.

**Common errors**

- “No service is set up for reading”: Enter the address under Connections → Reading mail and photos and test the connection.
- The document has no text layer: **It is a scan.** Enter it by hand; the PDF stays as a record.
- No answer within the time limit: **The first read after a pause loads the model into memory first.** Try again.

[Inbox](../anleitungen/posteingang.md) · [Set up Ollama](../anleitungen/texterkennung.md#set-up-ollama) · [Where your data stays](../anleitungen/posteingang.md#privacy-what-goes-where)

<a id="weg-home-assistant"></a>

## With Home Assistant

Home Assistant delivers the readings, the Energietracker calculates and reports back.

<picture><source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="../../ui/wegweiser/home-assistant.en.narrow.svg"><img src="../../ui/wegweiser/home-assistant.en.svg" alt="Diagram: With Home Assistant" width="760"></picture>

**Inside your home**

- Smart meters → Home Assistant: meter readings
- Home Assistant → Energietracker: readings, daily or per quarter-hour
- Energietracker → Home Assistant: sensors, notices, dates
- evcc → Energietracker: charging sessions
- You → Energietracker: contracts, analyses

**Across the boundary of your home**

- Energietracker → Weather service: rounded location, can be switched off

**Who it is for:** For anyone already using Home Assistant or wanting to read smart meters. The Energietracker reads no meters itself; Home Assistant does that.

**What you get**

- Readings arrive by themselves, daily or every 15 minutes.
- With values per quarter-hour, also the analyses of flexibility and storage.
- **Back in Home Assistant:** sensors for balance, consumption, forecast and “To do”, without YAML through the HACS integration.
- Notifications about deadlines and new documents, plus dates as a calendar.
- With evcc, the wallbox’s charging sessions including the solar share.

**What you need**

- Software: **Home Assistant.** The Energietracker as an app in Home Assistant OS (experimental) or as its own container. For the sensors, the HACS integration, from Home Assistant 2026.3.
- Hardware: **What Home Assistant needs anyway, plus your smart meters or readers.** As an app, the Energietracker needs no device of its own.

**Effort:** **Create a token, give meters an alias, add a REST command and an automation.** That is YAML; anyone who knows Home Assistant will find their way quickly. The way back through the integration needs no YAML.

**Steps**

1. **Start the Energietracker:** as an app in Home Assistant OS or as its own container. [App in Home Assistant](../anleitungen/home-assistant.md#as-an-app-in-home-assistant-os) · [Docker](../betrieb/docker.md)
2. Under Connections → Home Assistant, create the token and give the meters an alias. (in the app: **Home Assistant**)
3. Add the REST command and the automation in Home Assistant. [Connect Home Assistant](../anleitungen/home-assistant.md#step-3--rest-command-in-home-assistant)
4. Install the HACS integration for the sensors. [HACS integration](../anleitungen/home-assistant.md#hacs-integration-v3120)
5. **If you like:** switch on notifications. [Notifications](../anleitungen/home-assistant.md#step-6--notifications-to-home-assistant-v390)
6. **With a wallbox:** add evcc. [Charging sessions from evcc](../anleitungen/evcc.md)

**Where your data stays:** **Everything stays on your home network:** Home Assistant and the Energietracker talk directly. The app only sends notifications once someone who manages the installation switches them on, and only to your Home Assistant. The weather sync is the same for every way.

**What it cannot do**

- The Energietracker controls nothing. evcc or Home Assistant control the wallbox and storage; it does the sums.
- **The unit must match:** what Home Assistant delivers must fit the meter’s unit, or the readings will be wrong.
- Heating oil and pellets work with deliveries and do not go through this entrance.

**In detail:** **Home Assistant sends the readings with `POST /api/ingest` and a token (`et_…`).** On the way back it reads `/api/summary` and `/api/todo`; with sign-in on, that takes a read key, the token does not apply there.

**Addresses and ports**

- Home Assistant → Energietracker: `http://energietracker.local:8080/api.php/api/ingest`. With `api.php` it always works; with a rewrite rule in the web server, also without.
- Energietracker → sensors: `http://energietracker.local:8080/api/summary`. The integration asks every 15 minutes and creates the sensors itself.
- App in Home Assistant, from outside it: `http://homeassistant.local:8095`. **The sidebar runs through Ingress.** For other programs, open a port in the app under Configuration → Network, such as `8095`.

**Start of the REST command**

```text
rest_command:
  energietracker_push:
    url: "http://energietracker.local:8080/api.php/api/ingest"
    method: POST
    headers:
      Authorization: !secret energietracker_auth
      Content-Type: "application/json"
```

**Good to know**

- **`!secret` only works as a whole value.** So `secrets.yaml` holds `"Bearer et_…"` including `Bearer`.
- Home Assistant’s “Model Context Protocol” integration does not work: it only speaks SSE.
- Anything that can send an HTTP request delivers through the same entrance, including ioBroker, Node-RED and openHAB.

**Common errors**

- `401` in the Home Assistant log: **Wrong token or missing header.** Use `Authorization: !secret energietracker_auth` as a whole value.
- `400`, no meter found: **The alias does not match the meter.** Check it in the settings.
- The value arrives but does not count: **It is lower than the previous reading and therefore flagged as suspect.** Check it in the utility’s view.

[Connect Home Assistant](../anleitungen/home-assistant.md) · [Charging sessions from evcc](../anleitungen/evcc.md) · [ioBroker, Node-RED, openHAB](../anleitungen/andere-systeme.md)

<a id="weg-local-ai"></a>

## With local AI

You ask in your own words. Model and figures stay at home.

<picture><source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="../../ui/wegweiser/local-ai.en.narrow.svg"><img src="../../ui/wegweiser/local-ai.en.svg" alt="Diagram: With local AI" width="760"></picture>

**Inside your home**

- You → Open WebUI: you ask
- Open WebUI → You: answer
- Open WebUI → Ollama: question and figures
- Ollama → Open WebUI: text of the answer
- Open WebUI → Energietracker: looks it up: MCP with a key
- Energietracker → Open WebUI: figures with their source
- You → Energietracker: confirm a change in the app

**Across the boundary of your home**

- Model download → Ollama: load the model, once during setup
- Energietracker → Weather service: rounded location, can be switched off

**Who it is for:** For anyone who wants to ask about their figures in their own words, without questions or figures leaving the house. You should not mind Docker, or have someone who helps with the setup.

**What you get**

- Answers to questions like “What is my gas balance?”, with the same figures as in the app.
- **The source of every figure:** measured, entered, spread, assumed or estimated.
- Ready-made tasks for the monthly report, annual report, bill check and deadlines.
- **Proposals instead of changes:** the AI enters nothing itself, you confirm in the app.

[What does it do for you?](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#mehrwert) · [Who confirms a change?](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#wer-bestaetigt)

**What you need**

- Software: Energietracker from v3.12.0, Docker with Open WebUI 0.6.31 or later in it, plus Ollama with a model that can use tools. Exactly this combination has been tested: Open WebUI with local Ollama. Other local programs are experimental.
- Hardware: A computer with plenty of memory, ideally with a GPU the model can use. The smaller the computer, the longer an answer takes. The Energietracker may run on another device on your home network.

**Effort:** **More than one installation:** three programs, a large download for the model and a connection you enter. After that you just ask. How long an answer takes depends on model and computer; the guide gives measured values.

**Steps**

1. The Energietracker runs on your home network. [By hand](#weg-by-hand)
2. **Install Ollama and get a model that can use tools.** The guide shows the installation with an image model; here, take a language model with the `tools` capability. [Set up Ollama](../anleitungen/texterkennung.md#set-up-ollama)
3. Start Open WebUI in a container. [Open WebUI: quick start](https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/)
4. Under Connections, open the “AI assistants (MCP)” card, choose “Switch on the AI interface” and create a “AI read” key. (in the app: **AI assistants (MCP)**) · [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#step-2--create-a-key)
5. In Open WebUI, as an administrator, add the Energietracker as a tool server: type MCP (Streamable HTTP), address and key. [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#open-webui)
6. Switch the tool on in the chat and ask. [Example questions](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#examples)

**Where your data stays:** **Question, figures and answer stay on your home network: Ollama runs on your computer.** That holds as long as you add no cloud model and no web search in Open WebUI. Only the programs and the model come from the internet, once. The AI gets identifiers and originals only with the switches “Give identifiers to the AI” and “Give originals to the AI”; both are off by default. The weather sync is the same for every way.

**What it cannot do**

- **The AI does not calculate, it tells.** It can get things wrong while doing so. Check important figures in the app.
- **No tools for settings, people, keys, backups or deleting.** That stays in the app.
- Long extractions with a local model and reports as PDF stay in the app.
- Programs that only speak SSE or insist on OAuth do not connect.
- The public demo has no AI interface, because it runs without a server.

**In detail:** **The usual setup:** Open WebUI in a container, Ollama natively on the computer, the Energietracker on the same computer or the NAS. Open WebUI is the hub: it sends your question to Ollama and calls the Energietracker’s tools itself. The model never talks to the Energietracker directly.

**Addresses and ports**

- Browser → Open WebUI: `http://mein-rechner.local:3000`. Port 3000 on the computer leads to port 8080 in the container.
- Open WebUI → Ollama: `http://host.docker.internal:11434`. **Inside the container, `localhost` is the container itself.** Unless told otherwise, Open WebUI looks for Ollama at this address.
- Open WebUI → Energietracker on the same computer: `http://host.docker.internal:8080/api/mcp`. **This is the address you enter in Open WebUI.** It only accepts `POST` with a key, so testing in a browser does not help.
- Open WebUI → Energietracker on another device with Docker: `http://energietracker.local:8080/api/mcp`. With that device’s address on your home network.
- Open WebUI → Energietracker on Apache or Synology Web Station: `http://energietracker.local/energietracker/api.php/api/mcp`. **Here `api.php` belongs in the address.** The “AI assistants (MCP)” card always shows the address with `api.php`; it works with every web server.

**Template based on the manufacturers’ guides**

```text
services:
  energietracker:
    image: ghcr.io/bingerminger/energietracker:3
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["8080:80"]
    volumes: ["./data:/data"]
  open-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    restart: always
    ports: ["3000:8080"]
    environment:
      WEBUI_SECRET_KEY: "<openssl rand -hex 32>"
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    volumes: ["open-webui:/app/backend/data"]
volumes:
  open-webui:
```

**Good to know**

- On a Mac, Ollama runs as its own program next to Docker, not in a container: Docker Desktop does not pass the GPU through. That is what Ollama says. On Linux with an Nvidia card, the `ollama/ollama` container works too.
- **`host.docker.internal` points to the computer under Docker Desktop (Mac, Windows).** On Linux the name only exists with `extra_hosts`, as in the file above.
- **Keys:** “AI read” may use all reading tools, prompts and resources. “AI read and propose” may also read documents and propose changes. Start with “AI read”. The app shows the key (`etk_…`) only once; other keys do not work here.
- **“Confirm changes in the app only” is on by default: even if the AI wants to apply a change, it writes nothing.** You confirm the proposal under “To do”.
- **The interface is off by default.** `ET_MCP=off` locks it firmly, even if someone flips the switch.

**Common errors**

- `401`: **No key, or a wrong one.** Create revoked keys again.
- `403`, the interface is off: The “Switch on the AI interface” switch is off, or `ET_MCP=off` is set.
- `403` with `insufficient_scope`: The key has no AI scope, or a proposing tool was called with “AI read”.
- `404`: **Wrong address.** On Apache and Synology, `api.php` belongs in it.
- `421`: You have set a host list (`ET_ALLOWED_HOSTS` or under Settings → Access and security), and `host.docker.internal` is not on it.
- Open WebUI shows no models: **Is Ollama running?** If the container cannot get through, set `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` (on a Mac with `launchctl setenv`) and restart Ollama. Ollama has no sign-in: do not expose the port to the internet.
- No tools in the chat: **Reload the page and switch the tool on in the chat.** The model must have the `tools` capability.

[Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md) · [Open WebUI: MCP](https://docs.openwebui.com/features/extensibility/mcp) · [Ollama: Docker and GPU](https://ollama.com/blog/ollama-is-now-available-as-an-official-docker-image)

<a id="weg-cloud-ai"></a>

## With cloud AI (experimental)

The model runs at the provider. What it reads leaves your home.

<picture><source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="../../ui/wegweiser/cloud-ai.en.narrow.svg"><img src="../../ui/wegweiser/cloud-ai.en.svg" alt="Diagram: With cloud AI (experimental)" width="760"></picture>

**Inside your home**

- You → AI program: you ask
- AI program → You: answer
- AI program → Energietracker: looks it up: MCP with a key
- Energietracker → AI program: figures with their source
- You → Energietracker: confirm a change in the app

**Across the boundary of your home**

- AI program → Model provider: question and the tools’ answers
- Model provider → AI program: text of the answer
- Energietracker → Weather service: rounded location, can be switched off

**Who it is for:** For anyone without a computer for a local model who deliberately decides that figures may leave the house.

**What you get**

- The same figures with their source as on the local way.
- No computer of your own for the model.
- “Confirm changes in the app only” stays on: the AI cannot change anything without you.

[Who confirms a change?](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#wer-bestaetigt)

**What you need**

- Software: Energietracker from v3.12.0, an AI program with MCP over HTTP that can send a key, and an account with the model provider. All these routes are experimental: they follow the manufacturers’ guides and we have not tested them.
- Hardware: An ordinary computer is enough; the model runs at the provider.

**Effort:** **Set up one program and enter the key.** On top come costs with the provider, at its prices.

**Steps**

1. The Energietracker runs on your home network. [By hand](#weg-by-hand)
2. Choose a program that runs on your computer and speaks MCP over HTTP. [Programs](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#programme)
3. Under Connections, open the “AI assistants (MCP)” card, choose “Switch on the AI interface” and create a “AI read” key. (in the app: **AI assistants (MCP)**) · [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#step-2--create-a-key)
4. Connect the program as the guide shows for yours. [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#other-programs-experimental)
5. Read what goes out and check the provider’s terms. [Where your data stays](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#security-and-privacy)

**Where your data stays:** What the AI reads, the model provider sees: your questions and the tools’ answers, meaning figures on consumption, costs and contracts. Passwords and keys, settings with network addresses, the list of people, backups and logs never leave. Identifiers and originals only with the switches “Give identifiers to the AI” and “Give originals to the AI”; both are off by default. The weather sync is the same for every way.

**What it cannot do**

- **Programs that connect from their provider’s cloud cannot reach your home network.** That only works by following the guide, with your own HTTPS access, and it puts an entry point on the internet.
- **No OAuth:** programs that insist on OAuth sign-in do not connect.
- **No tools for settings, people, keys, backups or deleting.** That stays in the app.
- **Experimental means:** feedback is welcome, and things may change.

**In detail:** Examples of such programs, all experimental: Claude Code, VS Code (Copilot Chat) and Cursor on your computer. The program talks to the Energietracker on your home network and sends what it reads to its model.

**Addresses and ports**

- AI program on your computer → Energietracker: `http://energietracker.local:8080/api/mcp`. On Apache and Synology, `api.php` belongs in the address.
- Service from the cloud → your own HTTPS access: `https://energie.example.org/api/mcp`. **Only if the service allows its own header with the key.** The reverse proxy lets only `/api/mcp` through. This is a guide, not a recommendation.

**Good to know**

- **Create a separate key for each program and device.** Start with “AI read”; “AI read and propose” may also propose.
- A cloud model in Open WebUI is also experimental: the data then goes to the provider.
- **Revoke the key as soon as you no longer need the access.** Rate limits and the lockout after wrong keys apply here too.

**Common errors**

- `401`: **No key, or a wrong one.** Some programs then look for an OAuth sign-in and report an error about it; the cause is still the key.
- `403`, the interface is off: The “Switch on the AI interface” switch is off, or `ET_MCP=off` is set.
- `404`: **Wrong address.** On Apache and Synology, `api.php` belongs in it.

[From the cloud: your own HTTPS access](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md#from-the-cloud-only-with-your-own-https-access) · [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](../anleitungen/ki-assistent.md)

<a id="weg-together"></a>

## All together

The building blocks complement each other, and none depends on another.

<picture><source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="../../ui/wegweiser/together.en.narrow.svg"><img src="../../ui/wegweiser/together.en.svg" alt="Diagram: All together" width="760"></picture>

**Inside your home**

- Home Assistant → Energietracker: readings, daily or per quarter-hour
- Energietracker → Home Assistant: sensors, notices, dates
- Supplier mail → Energietracker: drop the PDF
- AI at home → Energietracker: looks it up: MCP with a key
- Energietracker → AI at home: figures with their source
- You → Energietracker: confirm a change in the app
- You → AI at home: you ask

**Across the boundary of your home**

- Energietracker → Cloud service: only what you explicitly switch on
- Energietracker → Weather service: rounded location, can be switched off

**Who it is for:** For anyone who wants to combine several ways. You need not set everything up at once; each block runs on its own, and the order does not matter.

**What you get**

- Home Assistant delivers the readings; the mail delivers contracts and bills.
- The app checks the bill from the mail against your readings.
- The AI asks for everything in one place and gives the source of every figure.
- By hand always remains possible, for instance for the meter without a sensor.

**What you need**

- Software: What the individual ways need, nothing more.
- Hardware: **One computer can carry a lot:** Open WebUI in a container, Ollama natively, the Energietracker on the same computer or the NAS.

**Effort:** The sum of the blocks, but step by step: you start with one and add the next when you need it.

**Steps**

1. The Energietracker runs. [By hand](#weg-by-hand)
2. Add readings from Home Assistant. [With Home Assistant](#weg-home-assistant)
3. Put the mail into the inbox. [With supplier mail](#weg-inbox)
4. Connect an AI, local or in the cloud. [With local AI](#weg-local-ai) · [With cloud AI (experimental)](#weg-cloud-ai)

**Where your data stays:** **What you do not explicitly send out stays inside.** Only three things can leave: the weather sync (rounded location, can be switched off), documents to a cloud service (after asking) and what a cloud AI reads (only if you connect one).

**What it cannot do**

- More blocks mean more programs to keep up to date.
- The Energietracker controls nothing, not even together with the others.
- **An AI does not replace checking:** you confirm what it proposes, and you look up important figures in the app.

**In detail:** **Every block has its address.** Replace the placeholders with yours.

**Addresses and ports**

- Energietracker: `http://energietracker.local:8080`. In the Docker image; on Apache and Synology without a port, in the app’s folder.
- Open WebUI: `http://mein-rechner.local:3000`. The chat in a browser.
- Ollama: `http://mein-rechner.local:11434`. **Has no sign-in:** do not expose the port to the internet.
- Home Assistant: `http://homeassistant.local:8123`. From inside a container, a name ending in `.local` often does not resolve; then enter the address on your home network.

**Good to know**

- **Every access has its own key:** the token (`et_…`) for readings from Home Assistant, a read key for the sensors, an AI key per AI program. None works for everything.
- As soon as several devices have access, switch on sign-in: Settings → Access and security.
- The use cases show ready-made combinations, such as wallbox and heat pump.
